transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2026-05-14 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 56 minutes
- Attendees: Jared, Priya, Marco (Redwood); Alex, Lina, Samir, Priya P. (Valence)

[00:00] Jared: Hi everyone, thanks for squeezing this in. I'm Jared from Redwood, AE on the account. Joining me is Priya our SE and Marco from CSM. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Alex: Good, hey Jared. We're excited to scope this POC, we've been looking at a couple vendors so want to get timelines locked down.
[00:11] Lina: Yeah hi, quick note, we'll be focused on R&D workflows — high token per request but not crazy qps.
[00:18] Priya: Great, that's helpful. Before we dive, quick agenda: agree success criteria, confirm workload sizing, outline benchmarks and deliverables, and map a 6-week timeline with checkpoints. Fine?
[00:28] Alex: Sounds good.
[00:30] Jared: Cool. First — success criteria. What would count as success for you at exec readout?
[00:36] Lina: For us the top line is quality preservation — our LLM-driven assay annotation needs to match current manual accuracy within a small delta, call it 3% top-line. Also we need predictable latency for interactive tooling, p95 under 450ms ideally.
[00:48] Priya Singh: Understood. Any hard constraints on PL/PD or data residency?
[00:52] Samir: Yes, must remain within our EU region for the pilot data, and all secrets go through our KMS. We'll need audit logs shipped to our SIEM. SOC2 is table stakes.
[01:03] Jared: Noted. We can support KMS integrations and S3/VPC peering for Private, or dedicated for Redwood Dedicated. For the POC we typically run hosted but with VPC egress to customer's S3 or a secure transfer.
[01:16] Alex: Can you clarify the difference operationally? Our infra team wants minimal change.
[01:20] Priya: Sure — hosted API means easiest onboarding; we'll ask for a whitelist and sample dataset upload. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and isolation but requires provisioning and lead time. For this POC, given low QPS but higher tokens, hosted with VPC storage access seems fastest.
[01:36] Lina: That makes sense. Timeline question: how long to get VPC access configured?
[01:39] Marco: Typical window is 3–7 business days once we have network details and contact. If Samir can provide the peering request and firewall rules today, we can start the ticketing flow.
[01:49] Samir: I can do that but need Redwood's network diagram and the specific IP ranges.
[01:53] Jared: We'll send the diagram and IP list in the access matrix after the call.
[01:57] Alex: OK. Next, workload sizing: Lina mentioned high tokens per request — can you quantify?
[02:03] Lina: Most requests are 3–5k tokens in payload, responses average 1.5–2k tokens. Peak parallelism is low, maybe 8 concurrent workers at most during batch runs; interactive tooling sees spikes of ~20 concurrent during demos.
[02:19] Priya: That helps. For benchmarking we'll create two profiles: interactive (p95 latency target 450ms at 20 concurrent) and batch (throughput, tokens/sec baseline for cost modeling). We'll instrument KV cache and prefix caching to lower cost on repeat prompts.
[02:33] Alex: Question: what's realistic p95 for a 5k token input on your hosted models?
[02:37] Priya: For unquantized 7B-ish models on NVNe GPUs p95 for 5k can range 350–800ms depending on batching; bigger models go higher. We'll propose a model matrix in the sizing spreadsheet so you can pick latency vs quality tradeoffs.
[02:51] Lina: We also need to cap cost — target is under $X per 1k tokens for gen and embeddings for the pilot.
[02:56] Jared: We'll model cost-per-1k tokens across a couple model families and quantization profiles — that's in the playbook.
[03:02] Alex: Benchmarks — what's the plan?
[03:04] Priya: Bench plan: 1) Synthetic ramp to establish p95/p50 at target concurrency; 2) Real sample set (anonymized) run to evaluate quality and token footprint; 3) Long tail stress to expose degradation and cache hit rates. We'll output latency distributions, throughput, and cost-per-1k.
[03:22] Samir: For the security review, we need to validate that logs are immutable and that you support customer-managed KMS.
[03:28] Jared: We support both customer-managed KMS and detailed audit logs. We'll include SOC2 excerpts and a network diagram. Samir, Priya P., I'll loop you into the security doc share.
[03:37] Priya: One operational note — for KV cache, if you want to preserve session state between calls we'll need to scope TTLs. That impacts cost and memory usage on the runtime.
[03:47] Lina: TTL of 12 hours is fine for our use case.
[03:50] Priya: Great. On milestones, propose a six-week cadence: Week 0 kick off + access; Week 1 access validation and synthetic benchmark baseline; Week 3 mid-point review with quality signal and perf numbers; Week 5 optimization sprint; Week 6 exec readout.
[04:05] Alex: Week 3 mid-point — what do you expect from us?
[04:09] Priya: By mid-point we aim to have run the real-sample benchmark, produced a quality report (precision/recall or whatever metric you use), and cost estimates. We'll pair with your ML lead for any prompt tuning.
[04:20] Alex: Sounds reasonable.
[04:22] Marco: We'll also include a roll-back plan for the demo if any anomalies are found; basically fallback to smaller model or cached outputs.
[04:29] Lina: What about stakeholders at exec readout? Who should attend?
[04:32] Alex: We'll invite product leadership and ops — Lina and I will coordinate.
[04:36] Samir: One gating risk — our procurement requires a checklist for external data transfers. We'll need legal sign-off to run the sample data even if anonymized.
[04:45] Jared: We'll provide a minimal data handling agreement and a sample anonymization checklist.
[04:49] Priya: Ok let's capture the concrete acceptance criteria we heard: 1) Quality delta from manual <=3% on chosen metrics; 2) Interactive p95 <=450ms at up to 20 concurrent; 3) Cost target <= your provided token budget; 4) Security: KMS and audit logs in place.
[05:06] Lina: Yes that matches. I'd add that any model regression triggers a pause and joint triage — we want a clear rollback gate.
[05:13] Jared: Agreed, we'll include a gate in the playbook.
[05:16] Alex: One more practical: who will run the bench scripts? Redwood or Valence infra?
[05:19] Priya: We'll provide the scripts and can run the baseline if you prefer. Ideally we run initial synthetic runs, then hand over to your infra for the real-sample runs so numbers reflect your environment.
[05:31] Alex: We'll probably run both; your initial run helps accelerate.
[05:34] Jared: Great. I'll summarize next steps and owners in an email after the call.
[05:38] Priya: Action items recap: we'll send playbook, benchmark scripts, and access matrix. Valence to provide anonymized sample and network details.
[05:47] Samir: I'll prioritize the peering request, but need your diagram and exact egress IPs.
[05:52] Jared: We'll attach that in the access spreadsheet.
[05:56] Alex: Any other questions?
[05:58] Lina: No, thanks all.
[06:00] Jared: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the deck and schedule the mid-point in the calendar.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker overlap labeled generically; some proper nouns may be mis-transcribed (KMS sometimes as 'K M S'), model names abbreviated.
